The presence of a lowest common ancestor at the Nitrogen Molecular Entity implies a shared structural or functional role in the pathway. While the exact mechanism by which Nicardipine influences Angina Pectoris Aggravated remains unclear, the observed sequence of interactions suggests that Nicardipine may act as a modulator of Tiotropium's effect on Chrm5. This pathway highlights a potential role for Nicardipine in regulating Chrm5 activity, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct involvement of Nicardipine in this process.
